text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THAWRA
- Militants of the (ruling) Arab Baath Socialist Party in Baghdad perform an emergency exercise for the service of the people and the victorious march led by leader President Saddam Hussein.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz arrives in Brussels for talks with Belgian officials on disarmament and relations with U.N. Security Council.
- Revolutionary Command Council (RCC) ratifies law for the protection of environment.
- RCC issues decree allowing confiscation of unlicensed video-tapes in Iraq.
- First food shipments under oil-for-food deal with the United Nations are expected to reach Iraq next Tuesday.
- Foreign Undersecretary Saad al-Feisal continues talks with Turkish officials in Ankara to develop bilateral ties.
- Vietnamese deputy prime minister arrives in Baghdad to review trade relations.
- Iraqi-Russian joint committee starts meetings in Baghdad.
- National Assembly rejects Israeli projects to "Juadise" Jerusalem.
- Israeli bulldozers break ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab Jerusalem.
- Russia satisfied with Iraq-U.N. cooperation on disarmament.
- (The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and JUMHOURIYA)
- American professors among them Noam Chomsky voice concern for the suffering of Iraqi people.
- Arab federation of maritime transport to hold meeting in Baghdad.
- Commentary attacks Israel's decision to set up new settlement in Jerusalem.
- Article on media tactics used by the United States during the 1991 Gulf War to mislead world public opinion.
JUMHOURIYA
- Senior oil official says world will need at least eight million barrels of Iraqi oil per day in five years time.
- New irrigation projects in the southern province of Missan.
